examples.en: An excavator is digging the ground at the construction site.

examples.ko: 포클레인 소리 때문에 낮잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't nap because of the excavator noise.
My father works driving an excavator.

examples.ko: 길 옆에 큰 포클레인 한 대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A big excavator is parked beside the road.

examples.ko: 포클레인으로 파면 하루 만에 끝날 거예요.
examples.en: If we dig with an excavator, it will be done in a day.

examples.ko: 어린 아들이 장난감 포클레인만 가지고 놀아요.
examples.en: My little son only plays with his toy excavator.

explain: 공식적인 글에서는 '굴착기'라고 하고, 말할 때는 '포클레인'이라고 하는 사람이 많아요. 땅을 파는 기계라서 '포클레인으로 파다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In formal writing the word is '굴착기', but many people say '포클레인' when they talk. Since it is a digging machine, it goes naturally with phrases like '포클레인으로 파다' (to dig with an excavator).

en: go on a binge; eat too much

examples.en: When I'm stressed, I binge eat without realizing it.
I binged on a late-night meal last night and regretted it.

examples.ko: 다이어트 중에 참다가 결국 폭식을 하고 말았어요.
examples.en: I held out during my diet but ended up bingeing anyway.

examples.ko: 밤마다 이어지는 폭식 때문에 몸무게가 많이 늘었어요.
examples.en: I gained a lot of weight because of nightly binge eating.

examples.ko: 너무 많이 폭식하면 속이 불편하니까 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: If you binge too much your stomach will hurt, so eat slowly.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝난 날 친구와 같이 폭식했어요.
examples.en: On the day the exam ended, I binged with my friend.

explain: '과식하다'는 그냥 많이 먹는 것이고, '폭식하다'는 짧은 시간에 멈추지 못하고 한꺼번에 먹는 느낌이 강해요. '음식을 폭식하다'보다 '폭식을 하다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '과식하다' just means eating too much, while '폭식하다' feels like eating a lot all at once and being unable to stop. People often say '폭식을 하다' rather than putting a food directly before '폭식하다'.

examples.en: This cushion is really soft and fluffy.

examples.ko: 폭신폭신한 이불에 누우니까 바로 잠이 왔어요.
examples.en: I fell asleep right away lying on the fluffy blanket.
The freshly baked bread is soft and delicious.
The doll is so soft that it's comfortable to sleep hugging it.
The snow-covered path felt soft underfoot.

examples.ko: 폭신폭신할 것 같아서 이 소파를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought this sofa because it looked soft and cushiony.

explain: '폭신하다'를 반복해서 더 부드럽고 귀엽게 느껴지게 말하는 형태예요. 이불, 빵, 인형처럼 손으로 누르면 부드럽게 들어가는 것에 잘 써요. 반대로 단단한 느낌은 '딱딱하다'예요.
explain_en: This is a doubled form of '폭신하다' that sounds softer and cuter. It suits things that sink gently when pressed, such as blankets, bread and stuffed toys. The opposite feeling is '딱딱하다' (hard).

examples.ko: 이 침대는 폭신해서 자도 허리가 안 아파요.
examples.en: This bed is soft, so my back doesn't hurt after sleeping.
My feet feel comfortable in these soft slippers.
The cake sponge is very soft.
I wonder how to cook a fluffy rolled omelet.

examples.ko: 소파가 너무 폭신하면 오래 앉기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If a sofa is too soft, it's hard to sit for long.
The path covered in fallen leaves feels soft.

explain: '푹신하다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, '폭신하다'가 좀 더 가볍고 작은 느낌이에요. 사람의 성격이 아니라 침대, 빵, 눈길처럼 닿는 느낌에 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '푹신하다', but '폭신하다' feels a bit lighter and smaller. It describes how something feels to the touch, like beds, bread or snowy paths, not a person's personality.

examples.ko: 그는 회의 중에 갑자기 폭탄선언을 했어요.
examples.en: He suddenly dropped a bombshell during the meeting.
Everyone was shocked by the boss's sudden bombshell announcement.

examples.ko: 유명 배우의 결혼 폭탄선언이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A famous actor's surprise marriage announcement was in the news.

examples.ko: 폭탄선언은 가족과 미리 상의한 뒤에 하세요.
examples.en: Talk it over with your family before making a bombshell announcement.

examples.ko: 친구의 폭탄선언 뒤에 한참 동안 조용했어요.
examples.en: It was quiet for a long time after my friend's bombshell.

examples.ko: 딸이 퇴사하겠다고 폭탄선언해서 집이 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: My daughter shocked us by announcing she'd quit her job, and the house was in an uproar.

explain: 모두가 예상하지 못한 중요한 발표에 써요. 뉴스에서는 '폭탄 발언'이라고도 해요. 보통 '폭탄선언을 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for an important announcement nobody expected. News also uses '폭탄 발언' in a similar way. The usual pattern is '폭탄선언을 하다'.

examples.en: I add just a little bleach to white laundry.

examples.ko: 표백제를 쓸 때는 창문을 열어 주세요.
examples.en: Please open the windows when you use bleach.

examples.ko: 이 표백제는 색깔 있는 옷에 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use this bleach on colored clothes.
It is dangerous to mix bleach with other detergents.
I wiped the bathroom mold clean with bleach.

examples.ko: 표백제 냄새가 너무 독해서 머리가 아파요.
examples.en: The bleach smell is so strong that I get a headache.

explain: 옷을 희게 하거나 얼룩, 곰팡이를 없애는 약품이에요. 집에서는 염소계 표백제를 흔히 '락스'라고 불러요. '표백제'는 포장이나 설명서에 쓰인 말에 가까워요. 옷에는 '산소계 표백제'처럼 종류를 붙여 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a chemical that whitens clothes or removes stains and mold. At home, chlorine bleach is commonly called '락스'. '표백제' sounds closer to the wording on labels and instructions. Types are named too, as in '산소계 표백제' (oxygen-based bleach).

examples.ko: 길가에 공사 중이라는 푯말이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A sign saying 'under construction' stands by the road.
I followed the signpost and took the right road.
They put up a sign telling people to keep off the grass.

examples.ko: 푯말에 적힌 글씨가 흐려서 안 보여요.
examples.en: The writing on the sign is faded and I can't read it.

examples.ko: 등산로마다 푯말이 있어서 길을 잃지 않아요.
examples.en: Every hiking trail has signposts, so you don't get lost.

examples.ko: 밭 입구에 주인 이름을 적은 푯말도 있어요.
examples.en: There is also a sign with the owner's name at the field entrance.

explain: '표지판'과 비슷한데, 푯말은 말뚝이나 나무판에 글씨를 써서 세워 둔 작은 것을 떠올리게 해요. 도로나 건물의 공식 안내판은 '표지판'이 더 자연스러워요. '푯말을 세우다, 푯말이 서 있다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '표지판', but '푯말' suggests a small sign written on a stake or wooden board. For official road or building signs, '표지판' sounds more natural. It commonly goes with '푯말을 세우다' and '푯말이 서 있다'.

examples.en: Before sunrise, the dawn sky looks bluish.
After swimming for a long time, my lips turned bluish.
A bluish light comes into the room.
The photo came out bluish, so I took it again.
The lake in the moonlight looks so faintly blue.
The early morning mist was bluish and mysterious.

explain: 완전한 파란색이 아니라 연하게 푸른빛이 도는 색이에요. 새벽 하늘, 달빛, 추워서 변한 입술처럼 '살짝 푸르게 보이는' 때 써요. 비슷한 '파르스름하다'는 좀 더 맑고 연한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes a color that is faintly blue rather than fully blue. Use it for things that look slightly blue, like dawn skies, moonlight or cold lips. The similar '파르스름하다' feels a bit lighter and clearer.

examples.en: Even small change becomes big money when you save it.
My pay is low, so I save even the small amounts.
Small amounts keep leaving my wallet for coffee.
I saved up small amounts and took a family trip.

examples.ko: 이 정도는 푼돈이니까 신경 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: This is just pocket change, so don't worry about it.
I don't want to fight with a friend over a small sum.

explain: '잔돈'은 물건을 사고 거슬러 받는 돈이고, '푼돈'은 액수가 작은 돈 전체를 말해요. 반대말은 '목돈'이에요. '푼돈을 모으다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '잔돈' is the change you get back after paying, while '푼돈' means small amounts of money in general. Its opposite is '목돈' (a large lump sum). A common pattern is '푼돈을 모으다' (to save up small amounts).

examples.en: In winter I buy and eat pulppang on the street.
You pour batter into the mold and bake it.

examples.ko: 이 풀빵 속에는 팥이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This pulppang is full of red bean filling.

examples.ko: 퇴근길에 따뜻한 풀빵 한 봉지를 샀어요.
examples.en: On the way home from work I bought a bag of warm pulppang.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 학교 앞 풀빵이 제일 맛있었어요.
examples.en: As a kid, the pulppang in front of my school was the tastiest.
Pulppang is cheap, so it's easy on the wallet.

explain: 붕어빵, 국화빵처럼 틀에 반죽을 부어 구운 길거리 간식을 두루 가리킬 때가 있어요. 가게나 지역에 따라 부르는 이름이 다를 수 있어요. 겨울 간식으로 많이 떠올려요.
explain_en: It can refer broadly to street snacks baked from batter in a mold, like 붕어빵 and 국화빵. The name people use may differ by shop or region. Many Koreans think of it as a winter snack.

examples.ko: 오늘 사회 시간에 풀뿌리 민주주의를 배웠어요.
examples.en: Today in social studies we learned about grassroots democracy.
They say that in the old days, people were so poor they ate grass roots.
I had a hard time pulling grass roots in the garden.
A grassroots group helps with the village cleanup.

examples.ko: 잡초는 풀뿌리까지 뽑아야 다시 안 나요.
examples.en: Weeds won't come back unless you pull them out by the roots.
A grassroots citizens' movement changed the policy.

explain: 풀의 뿌리라는 뜻으로도 쓰지만 뉴스에서는 '일반 시민이 중심이 되는'이라는 뜻으로 더 자주 나와요. '풀뿌리 민주주의', '풀뿌리 단체'처럼 뒤에 명사가 붙어요.

phrases.example: 지역 주민이 직접 참여하는 것이 풀뿌리 민주주의의 시작이에요.
phrases.en: Residents taking part directly is the start of grassroots democracy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주민과 시민이 직접 참여해 만드는 민주주의를 말해요. 뉴스와 수업에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to democracy built by residents and citizens taking part directly. It often appears in news and classes.

explain_en: It can mean the roots of grass, but in the news it more often means 'led by ordinary citizens'. It usually comes before a noun, as in '풀뿌리 민주주의' and '풀뿌리 단체'.

examples.ko: 여름밤에는 풀숲에서 곤충 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: On summer nights, loud insect sounds come from the grass thicket.
The ball rolled into the tall grass.

examples.ko: 풀숲을 헤치고 들어가 보니 작은 연못이 있었어요.
examples.en: When I pushed through the thicket, there was a small pond.

examples.ko: 풀숲에는 모기가 많으니까 긴 바지를 입으세요.
examples.en: There are many mosquitoes in the bushes, so wear long pants.
The cat disappeared into the bushes.

examples.ko: 키 큰 풀숲 속에 새 둥지가 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a bird's nest in the tall grass.

explain: 나무가 많은 '숲'과 달리, 풀이 빽빽하게 자란 곳에 써요. '수풀'과 비슷하게 쓰는데 일상 대화에서는 '풀숲'이 더 흔히 들려요. 벌레나 작은 동물이 숨는 곳으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '숲', which has many trees, '풀숲' is a place where grass grows thickly. It is used much like '수풀', and in everyday talk '풀숲' is the one you hear more. It often appears as a hiding place for insects and small animals.

examples.en: I put glue on the back of the paper and stuck it on.
The glue isn't even, so the photo is coming up.
Apply paste to the wallpaper, then put it up slowly.
With my earnings these days, it's hard even to scrape by.

examples.ko: 풀칠은 얇게 해야 종이가 안 구겨져요.
examples.en: Spread the glue thinly so the paper doesn't wrinkle.

examples.ko: 어렵게 살던 때에는 하루 한 끼로 겨우 입에 풀칠했대요.
examples.en: They say that in hard times they barely got by on one meal a day.

explain: 종이나 벽지에 풀을 바르는 일에 쓰고, '풀칠을 하다'나 '풀칠하다'라고 해요. '입에 풀칠하다'라는 말로 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I have no job, so it's hard even to make ends meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨우 굶지 않고 살아간다는 뜻이에요. 형편이 어려울 때 쓰고, 보통 '입에 풀칠하기도 어렵다'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means barely managing to eat and survive. It is used about hard circumstances, often as '입에 풀칠하기도 어렵다'.

explain_en: It is used for spreading paste on paper or wallpaper, as in '풀칠을 하다' or '풀칠하다'. You will often hear it in the expression '입에 풀칠하다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 품성이 따뜻해서 모두가 좋아해요.
examples.en: He has a warm character, so everyone likes him.

examples.ko: 아이의 품성은 가정 교육에서 많이 길러져요.
examples.en: A child's character is largely shaped by upbringing at home.

examples.ko: 좋은 품성을 가진 사람과 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with people of good character.
I heard interviewers look closely at an applicant's character too.
Thanks to his excellent character, he even received an award.
There is nothing to criticize about his character.

explain: '성격'은 밝다, 급하다처럼 타고난 기질까지 두루 말하지만, '품성'은 사람 됨됨이, 곧 인품과 도덕적인 면을 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '품성이 좋다, 바르다'처럼 칭찬하는 문장에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '성격' covers temperament in general, such as cheerful or hasty, but '품성' is about a person's moral character and quality. That is why it often appears in praise like '품성이 좋다' or '품성이 바르다'.

examples.en: The baby is sleeping soundly in its mother's arms.
It was cold, so the cat burrowed into my arms.
I hid the letter inside my coat and ran here in a hurry.
My mother's embrace was always warm.

examples.ko: 코트 품속이 넓어서 작은 책도 들어가요.
examples.en: The inside of the coat is roomy, so even a small book fits.

examples.ko: 어린 시절 아버지 품속의 냄새가 아직 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the smell of my father's embrace from childhood.

explain: '품'과 가깝지만 '품속'은 안겨 있는 가슴 안쪽이나 옷 안쪽을 더 구체적으로 느끼게 해요. 사람에게는 '엄마 품속, 품속에 안기다'처럼 따뜻한 느낌으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '품', but '품속' more concretely evokes the inner space of an embrace or the inside of clothing. For people it often has a warm feeling, as in '엄마 품속' and '품속에 안기다'.

examples.en: On the weekend I saw a beautiful landscape painting at the museum.
My grandfather paints landscapes as a hobby.

examples.ko: 이 풍경화는 가을 산을 그린 거예요.
examples.en: This landscape painting depicts an autumn mountain.
The lake in the landscape painting looks real.

examples.ko: 거실 벽에 풍경화 한 점을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I hung one landscape painting on the living room wall.
I like landscape paintings more than portraits.

explain: '풍경'은 눈에 보이는 경치이고, '풍경화'는 그것을 그린 그림이에요. 같이 알아 두면 좋은 그림 이름으로 '인물화', '정물화'가 있어요. '풍경화를 그리다, 풍경화를 걸다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '풍경' is scenery you see, and '풍경화' is a painting of it. Useful related painting types are '인물화' (portrait) and '정물화' (still life). It goes with verbs like '풍경화를 그리다' and '풍경화를 걸다'.

examples.en: The child jumped into the cool water with a splash.
The thrown stone plopped into the pond.
It's so hot that I want to plunge into the sea.
I accidentally dropped my phone into the toilet with a plop.
I was startled by a splash and turned around.
My friend dove into the pool with a big splash.

explain: 크고 무거운 것이 깊은 물에 떨어지는 소리와 모습에 써요. 작은 것이 떨어질 때는 '퐁당'을 써서 크기 느낌을 구별해요. 보통 '풍덩 빠지다, 풍덩 뛰어들다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It conveys the sound and look of something large and heavy dropping into deep water. For something small, people use '퐁당' instead, so the two differ in size feeling. It usually appears as '풍덩 빠지다' or '풍덩 뛰어들다'.

en: bumper crop; good harvest; good crop

examples.en: Apples had a bumper crop this year, so they are cheap.
The weather is good, so farmers expect a good harvest.
Thanks to the good harvest, the village held a feast.
When cabbage has a bumper crop, prices go down.
Even with a bumper crop, the farmers look gloomy.

examples.ko: 지난해 풍작에 이어 올해도 쌀농사가 잘됐어요.
examples.en: Following last year's bumper crop, rice farming went well this year too.

explain: 반대말은 '흉작'이에요. '풍년'은 농사가 잘된 해를 가리키고, '풍작'은 수확이 많은 것에 초점이 있어요. 풍작이면 값이 내려갈 수 있어서 뉴스에서 가격과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '흉작' (poor harvest). '풍년' refers to a year when farming went well, while '풍작' focuses on the large yield. A big harvest can lower prices, so it often appears in the news together with prices.

examples.en: Plane trees stand in a long row along the street.
In hot summer, the shade of a plane tree is cool.
In autumn, big plane tree leaves fall.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 플라타너스 아래에서 친구를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited for my friend under the plane tree in front of school.

examples.ko: 플라타너스 낙엽을 밟으면 바삭 소리가 나요.
examples.en: Stepping on plane tree leaves makes a crunchy sound.
Plane trees stand out because their bark is mottled.

explain: 한국 거리에서 가로수로 많이 볼 수 있는 큰 나무예요. 우리말로는 '버즘나무'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '플라타너스'라고 하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: It is a large tree often seen lining Korean streets. Its Korean name is also '버즘나무', but many people simply say '플라타너스' in daily talk.

examples.ko: 오랜 세월 피눈물을 흘리며 아이를 키우셨어요.
examples.en: For many years she raised her child through bitter hardship.

examples.ko: 저에게 피눈물 나게 한 사람을 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I can't forget the person who made me suffer so bitterly.
After painstaking effort, I passed.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 피눈물이 날 정도로 슬펐어요.
examples.en: That movie was so sad it was heartbreaking.
They say he was scammed and could only weep bitterly.
The daughter she raised through great hardship is finally graduating.

explain: 실제 피가 섞인 눈물보다는 아주 큰 고통, 억울함, 한을 나타내는 비유로 거의 써요. '피눈물을 흘리다, 피눈물이 나다'로 자주 말해요. 가볍게 힘든 일에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그 사람 때문에 피눈물 나는 시간을 보냈어요.
phrases.en: Because of that person, I went through a bitterly painful time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참기 힘든 고통이나 억울함을 아주 강하게 말해요. 무겁고 극적인 표현이라 일상의 사소한 일에는 어색해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It strongly expresses unbearable pain or resentment. It is heavy and dramatic, so it sounds odd for trivial everyday matters.

explain_en: It is almost always figurative, expressing great pain, injustice or deep sorrow rather than real bloody tears. It is common in '피눈물을 흘리다' and '피눈물이 나다'. Do not use it for mildly difficult things.

examples.en: This is money my parents earned with blood and sweat.

examples.ko: 피땀 어린 노력이 드디어 열매를 맺었어요.
examples.en: Their hard-won effort finally bore fruit.
This victory carries the players' blood and sweat.
I lost the money I saved through hard toil in a moment.
This is a project our team poured blood and sweat into.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 사장님의 피땀 덕분에 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: That shop became famous thanks to the owner's blood and sweat.

explain: 실제 피와 땀이라기보다 몹시 힘들게 애쓴 노력을 강조하는 말이에요. '피땀 흘리다'가 가장 자주 쓰이고 돈, 성과, 노력과 함께 나와요. 가벼운 일에는 너무 무거워 어색해요.

phrases.en: He grew the shop through sheer hard work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 상할 만큼 아주 열심히 노력한다는 비유예요. 성공이나 돈을 번 이야기와 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for working extremely hard. It often appears in stories about success or earning money.

explain_en: Rather than literal blood and sweat, it emphasizes extremely hard effort. '피땀 흘리다' is the most common form, and it goes with money, results and effort. It is too heavy for light matters.

examples.en: During summer vacation I caught a little minnow in the stream.

examples.ko: 물이 맑은 개울에는 피라미가 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many minnows live in clear streams.
The kids are chasing a school of minnows.
Minnows are small, so we let them go even after catching them.

examples.ko: 피라미 몇 마리가 돌 사이로 숨었어요.
examples.en: A few minnows hid between the stones.

examples.ko: 큰 물고기가 피라미를 쫓아 빠르게 헤엄쳐요.
examples.en: A big fish swims fast chasing the minnows.

explain: 강이나 개울에 사는 작은 민물고기예요. 사람에게 쓰면 힘이 약하고 보잘것없는 상대를 얕잡아 말하는 비유가 돼요. 이집트의 '피라미드'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그 정도 피라미는 상대하지 않는 편이에요.
phrases.en: I usually don't bother with small fry like that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이나 지위가 낮은 사람을 얕잡아 부르는 말이에요. 듣는 사람이 기분 나쁠 수 있어서 조심해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It belittles someone of low power or status. It can offend the listener, so use it carefully.

explain_en: It is a small freshwater fish living in rivers and streams. Applied to a person, it becomes a belittling figure of speech for someone weak or insignificant. It has nothing to do with '피라미드' (pyramid).

examples.en: I fell and got a bruise on my knee.
The spot I bumped on my arm turned into a dark bruise.
I put ice on my bruised leg.
It takes about a week for a bruise to fade.
A dark bruise even formed where I bumped yesterday.

examples.ko: 마음에 피멍이 들 만큼 힘든 시간이었어요.
examples.en: It was a time so hard that my heart felt bruised.

explain: 그냥 '멍'보다 피가 짙게 맺힌 심한 멍을 말할 때 써요. '피멍이 들다'가 가장 자연스러워요. '마음에 피멍이 들다'는 마음의 상처가 깊다는 비유예요.

phrases.example: 아이의 말 한마디에 마음에 피멍이 들었어요.
phrases.en: One remark from my child left my heart deeply hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 쌓인 아픔이나 큰 상처를 비유로 말해요. 감정이 무거운 말이라 가까운 사이나 글에서 주로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It figuratively describes long-built pain or a deep wound. The emotion is heavy, so it is used mainly with close people or in writing.

explain_en: It describes a deeper, darker bruise than a plain '멍'. '피멍이 들다' is the most natural pattern. '마음에 피멍이 들다' is a figure of speech meaning deep emotional hurt.

examples.ko: 방학이 되자 한적하던 해수욕장이 피서객으로 북적이기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Once vacation began, the quiet beach started to bustle with summer vacationers.

examples.ko: 해수욕장에는 피서객들의 안전을 위해 수영 금지선을 표시해 놓았어요.
examples.en: The beach has a swimming limit line marked for the safety of vacationers.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 홍수로 계곡 물이 넘쳐 피서객들이 대피했어요.
examples.en: A sudden flood made the valley overflow, and vacationers evacuated.

examples.ko: 주말 계곡은 피서객이 많아서 주차가 어려워요.
examples.en: On weekends the valley has many vacationers, so parking is hard.
Thanks to the summer vacationers, the seaside shops got busy.

examples.ko: 올여름은 비가 자주 와서 피서객이 줄었대요.
examples.en: I heard vacationers decreased because it rained often this summer.

explain: 더위를 피해 바다나 계곡으로 휴가를 간 사람을 말해요. '-객'이 붙은 '관광객, 등산객'과 같은 방식으로 이해하면 돼요. 뉴스에서는 해수욕장이나 계곡 소식과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to people who go to the sea or a valley to escape the heat. You can understand it like '관광객' and '등산객', which also end in '-객'. In the news it often appears with beach and valley reports.

examples.ko: 올여름 피서지로 강원도를 골랐는데 정말 시원해요.
examples.en: I chose Gangwon-do as my summer getaway, and it's really cool.

examples.ko: 이 계곡은 가까워서 피서지로서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This valley is close, so it is popular as a summer retreat.
In peak season, lodging at summer resorts is much more expensive.
Choosing a summer getaway is my biggest worry.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 매년 같은 피서지에 가요.
examples.en: My family goes to the same summer spot every year.

examples.ko: 유명한 피서지는 사람이 너무 많아서 피해요.
examples.en: I avoid famous summer spots because they're too crowded.

explain: 더위를 피해 가는 바다, 계곡, 산 같은 곳이에요. '휴양지'는 쉬러 가는 곳 전반이고, '피서지'는 여름철 더위를 피한다는 점이 분명해요. '피서지로 인기가 많다, 피서지를 고르다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means places like the sea, valleys and mountains that people go to in order to escape the heat. '휴양지' covers any place for rest, while '피서지' clearly relates to avoiding summer heat. It is common in '피서지로 인기가 많다' and '피서지를 고르다'.

en: with a light snort or chuckle; with a hiss

examples.ko: 친구 농담에 나도 모르게 피식 웃음이 나왔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't help chuckling at my friend's joke.

examples.ko: 그는 대답 없이 피식 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He just let out a small laugh without answering.
I chuckled to myself while reading a text message.

examples.ko: 어이가 없어서 피식 하고 웃음이 났어요.
examples.en: I was so dumbfounded that a little laugh slipped out.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 말을 듣고 피식 웃으시더니 넘어가셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher gave a little laugh at what I said and moved on.
The air leaked out of the balloon with a hiss.

explain: 소리를 거의 내지 않고 가볍게 웃을 때 써요. 재미있을 때도 쓰지만 어이없거나 비웃는 느낌일 수도 있어서 상황을 봐야 해요. 크게 웃을 때는 '깔깔'이나 '하하'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for a light laugh made with almost no sound. It can show amusement, but it can also feel dumbfounded or mocking, so check the situation. For loud laughter, use '깔깔' or '하하'.

examples.ko: 태풍으로 인한 피해액이 수백억 원에 달해요.
examples.en: The damage from the typhoon amounts to tens of billions of won.
The government is investigating the exact amount of damage.

examples.ko: 이번 화재의 피해액은 아직 정확하지 않아요.
examples.en: The damage amount of this fire is not yet exact.
Will the insurance company compensate the amount of the loss?
The aid money differs depending on the amount of damage.
Compensation starts only after the damage assessment is done.

explain: 손해를 돈으로 계산한 금액을 말해서 뉴스, 보험, 재난 기사에 자주 나와요. '피해액이 달하다, 피해액을 산정하다, 피해액을 집계하다'처럼 짝으로 익혀 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is the amount of loss counted in money, so it appears often in news, insurance and disaster reports. It is helpful to learn it in pairs like '피해액이 달하다', '피해액을 산정하다' and '피해액을 집계하다'.

examples.en: I carefully pulled out the splinter with tweezers.
Could you lend me tweezers?
I bought tweezers to shape my eyebrows.
I had no tweezers, so I picked it up with chopsticks.
The tips of the tweezers are sharp, so be careful.

examples.ko: 핀셋은 화장품 가게에서 쉽게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can easily buy tweezers at a cosmetics shop.

explain: 작은 것을 집는 도구인데, 뉴스에서는 '핀셋 지원, 핀셋 규제'처럼 필요한 곳만 정확히 골라 한다는 비유로도 많이 써요. 이런 때는 도구가 아니라 방식을 말하는 거예요.

phrases.example: 정부가 피해가 큰 업종에만 핀셋 지원을 하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The government decided to give targeted support only to the hardest-hit industries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓게 퍼뜨리지 않고 필요한 대상만 골라 정확히 한다는 뜻이에요. 주로 뉴스에서 지원, 규제, 방역 같은 말과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means choosing only the needed targets instead of spreading widely. It is mainly used in the news with words like support, regulation and quarantine.

explain_en: It is a tool for picking up small things, but in the news it is also used figuratively, as in '핀셋 지원' and '핀셋 규제', to mean targeting only exactly the needed spots. In those cases it describes a method, not the tool.

examples.en: My friend chided me for coming late.

examples.ko: 어머니는 제 방을 보고 핀잔을 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother scolded me when she saw my room.

examples.ko: 도와주지는 않고 핀잔만 주니까 화가 나요.
examples.en: He doesn't help and just criticizes, so I'm angry.
Please don't put people down in front of others.
The team leader told me off for the late report.
My younger sibling made a nagging remark and left.

explain: '야단치다'처럼 크게 혼내는 것이 아니라, 잘못이나 실수를 가볍게 꼬집으며 면박을 주는 말투예요. 보통 '핀잔을 주다'라고 띄어 쓰고, 듣는 쪽은 '핀잔을 듣다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '야단치다', it is not a loud scolding but a light jab that points out a mistake and makes the person feel small. It is usually written '핀잔을 주다' with a space, and the person on the receiving end says '핀잔을 듣다'.

examples.en: The photo came out blurry because it was out of focus.
Please set the camera focus on the face.

examples.ko: 네 질문은 핀트가 좀 어긋난 것 같아요.
examples.en: Your question seems a bit off the point.
It's easy to get the focus right with this lens.

examples.ko: 이 이야기의 핀트는 다른 데 있어요.
examples.en: The point of this story lies somewhere else.

examples.ko: 질문의 핀트에 맞게 답을 써야 점수를 받아요.
examples.en: You get points only if your answer matches the point of the question.

explain: 원래는 카메라의 초점이지만, 일상에서는 말이나 질문의 핵심이라는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. '핀트가 맞다, 핀트가 안 맞다, 핀트가 나가다'처럼 쓰고, 딱딱한 자리에서는 '초점'이나 '요점'이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 핀트가 안 맞는 대답을 해서 민망했어요.
phrases.en: I felt embarrassed because I gave an answer that missed the point.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 질문이나 상황의 핵심과 어긋난다는 뜻이에요. 사진과 상관없이 대화에서 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means what is said misses the core of the question or situation. It is a conversational figure of speech unrelated to photography.

explain_en: It originally means a camera's focus, but in daily talk it is often used for the core point of a statement or question. It appears as '핀트가 맞다', '핀트가 안 맞다' and '핀트가 나가다'. In formal settings '초점' or '요점' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 필기도구를 안 가져와서 친구에게 펜을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't bring writing supplies, so I borrowed a pen from my friend.
Bring only writing supplies to the exam room.
I had nothing to write with, so I took notes on my phone.
I put writing supplies and a notebook in my school bag.
I finished preparing my writing supplies last night.
Among writing instruments, a ballpoint pen is the most convenient.

explain: 연필, 볼펜, 샤프처럼 글씨를 쓰는 물건을 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '문구'는 가위, 풀, 공책까지 더 넓게 가리켜요. 시험 안내문에 '필기도구 지참'이라고 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It groups together things you write with, such as pencils, ballpoint pens and mechanical pencils. '문구' is broader and also includes scissors, glue and notebooks. Exam notices often say '필기도구 지참' (bring writing supplies).

examples.en: English cursive is hard to read.
My friend wrote me a card in cursive.
I bought a notebook to practice cursive.
Cursive looks pretty, so we decided to use it on the wedding invitation.
Please write in print instead of cursive.

examples.ko: 저는 영어 필기체에 아직 익숙하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm still not used to English cursive.

explain: 손으로 이어서 흘려 쓰는 글씨체를 말하고, 반대말은 '인쇄체'예요. 영어 알파벳 이야기에서 특히 자주 나오고, 한글은 '흘려 쓴 글씨'라고 하는 때도 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to handwriting where letters flow together, and its opposite is '인쇄체' (print style). It comes up especially when talking about the English alphabet, while for Hangul people often say '흘려 쓴 글씨' (hurriedly flowing writing).

examples.ko: 이 책은 신입 사원 필독서로 유명해요.
examples.en: This book is well known as a must-read for new employees.
The teacher gave us a required reading list for vacation.

examples.ko: 대학생이라면 꼭 읽어야 할 필독서가 있어요.
examples.en: There are must-read books every college student should read.

examples.ko: 필독서를 다 읽으려면 한 달은 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a month to finish all the required reading.
I bought it because it was called a must-read, but it's too hard.
This novel is on the must-read list for teenagers.

explain: '추천 도서'는 읽어 보라고 권하는 책이고, '필독서'는 꼭 읽어야 한다는 느낌이 강해요. 앞에 '청소년', '신입 사원', '방학'처럼 읽는 사람이나 때를 붙여서 자주 말해요.
explain_en: A '추천 도서' is a book recommended for you to read, while a '필독서' strongly feels like something you must read. It is often preceded by the readers or the time, as in '청소년', '신입 사원' and '방학'.
